analysis:
I found no concrete security regression in this batch. All changes sit in the T-059 account-erasure area (TB-006).

postgres/erasure.go:
- Confirm now revokes API keys and provider tokens through RevokedAt plus an AlreadyRevokedAt sentinel, replacing DeletedAt.
- CancelAccountErasure (~L253-272) now also restores API keys and provider tokens whose revocation matches open.RequestedAt. It requires RequestedAt to be non-nil.
- Credentials revoked before the confirm are meant to stay revoked via AlreadyRevokedAt. The SQL queries (RestoreAPIKeys, RestoreProviderTokens, SoftDelete*) and erasure.AlreadyRevokedAt were not supplied, so that guarantee is unverified.
- The T-059 mitigation text says only that the soft delete revokes credentials. It should record that cancel now reinstates the credentials the confirm revoked.
- The cache path for restored keys (the API key cache and CachedStore) was not reviewed.

memory/erasure_rules.go:
- New rules: app_attest_shadow_events (removes machineInventory.Events by erased provider session ID), request_rejections (clears the model and params fields, matched on ConsumerKeyHash), model_prices (deletes by AccountID) and app_attest_key_revocations (memoryNoTable).
- api_keys now also clears AllowedModels; stripe_withdrawals now also clears FailureReason.
- request_rejections relies on k.ConsumerKeyHash being non-empty, as the existing inference_routes rule does. NewKeys was not visible.

memory/machine_inventory.go:
- RecordAppAttestEvent now returns ErrErasureConflict for an erased provider session and lazily initialises the inventory. This removes a nil dereference and a post-erasure write path.

memory/erasure_keys.go: reviewed in full. It gives no sign of leaking shared SE or App Attest keys. Shared keys are excluded using erasedProviderLocked and erasedAccounts.

Not visible:
- erasure/rules.go, which must list the new rules for these memory entries to run.
- The Postgres counterparts for the new memory rules.
- The SQL migrations.
The next pass should confirm rule-table parity across backends and the SQL semantics of the AlreadyRevokedAt sentinel.
